title: Firecracker microVM REST API (over Unix socket)
summary: Firecracker is a VMM (Virtual Machine Monitor) for microVMs, written in Rust, used by AWS Lambda and Fargate. Its control API is a REST API over a Unix domain socket. Endpoints: PUT /machine-config, PUT /boot-source, PUT /drives/{id}, PUT /network-interfaces/{id}, PUT /vsock, PUT /actions (InstanceStart, SendCtrlAltDel, Pause, Resume, CreateSnapshot, LoadSnapshot, ...), GET /vm, GET /mmds, ... .
aliases: Firecracker microVM REST API (over Unix socket)

Endpoints: PUT /machine-config, PUT /boot-source, PUT /drives/{id}, PUT /network-interfaces/{id}, PUT /vsock, PUT /actions (InstanceStart, SendCtrlAltDel, Pause, Resume, CreateSnapshot, LoadSnapshot, ...), GET /vm, GET /mmds, ... .

structure.meaning: API listens on a Unix socket (path given by --api-sock). No TCP port.
MicroVM Metadata Service: GET/PUT /mmds (IMDSv2-like metadata for the guest, fetched via 169.254.169.254 inside the guest).

notes: Firecracker boots a microVM in ~125ms with <5MB memory overhead.
The jailer (firecracker-jailer) sets up a chroot, cgroup, and seccomp filter before exec'ing Firecracker.
Snapshot/restore enables sub-5ms cold starts by resuming from a saved state.
MMDS (MicroVM Metadata Service) is the guest-facing metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254), like AWS EC2 IMDS.
Firecracker uses KVM for hardware virtualization and virtio for I/O (net, blk, vsock, balloon, rng).
